criteria.evidence: cmdNew calls syncHeader; the AC1 CLI test checks the exact heading, blank line and status. The emoji test exercises all seven statuses.
writeField calls syncHeader. The AC2 integration test exercises missing-header repair, title changes and shipping to done.
lintTicket checks both rendered fields. The AC3 test exercises missing headers, stale titles and stale statuses.

splitHeader consumes body whitespace with its trailing \s*, and syncHeader replaces it with two newlines. The AC4 test checks content only from '## Problem' onwards for the live ticket, overlooking changes before that section.

findings.issue: Header repair does not preserve the remaining body. splitHeader's trailing \s* removes all whitespace before the first body content, including indentation. For example, a body beginning with an indented Markdown code block loses its indentation when init or set repairs the header, changing its meaning. Extra blank lines are also removed, contrary to criterion 4.
findings.suggested_fix: Identify header lines and their separators without consuming whitespace belonging to the remaining body. Add regression tests that compare the complete preserved body, including extra blank lines and an indented first content line.

product_md.note: The supplied living spec describes the intended capability and command behaviour accurately.

verdict.summary: The header creation, updates and lint warnings are covered by meaningful tests. Header repair can also remove whitespace from ticket content, so it needs a fix before merge. Independent command checks were blocked by the sandbox failing to start; this review relies on the supplied diff and test output.
